title: WPSS/1446/2013 of Smt Sudeshana Devi Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1446 OF 2013
Smt. Sudeshana Devi Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, Advocate, present for the petitioner
Mr. B.P.S. Mer, Brief Holder, present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioner is working as Auxiliary Nursing
Midwife (in short ëA.N.M.í) in a Government Hospital i.e
Community Health Centre, Jaspur, District Udham Singh
Nagar. The post of A.N.M. is a District cadre post. By the
impugned order dated 20/22.08.2013 Chief Medical
Officer, Udham Singh Nagar has transferred the petitioner
from Community Health Centre, Jaspur to Community
Health Centre, Khatima. The impugned order clearly
shows that the transfer has been made on ìAdministrative
groundsî.
2. The sole contention of the petitioner before this
Court is that her transfer has been made on Administrative
ground, but no reason has been assigned as to what
circumstance compelled the authorities, for making such a
transfer on Administrative grounds. He has relied upon
the Full Bench Judgment of this Court in Smt. Damyanti
Bisht Vs State of Uttarakhand & others (Special Appeal No.
143 of 2008) reported in 2008 (2) U.D. 517 wherein it has
been categorically held that though in an given
contingency, even on Administrative ground, transfer can
be made, but the competent authority, while doing so must

2
assigned reason for such transfer. The relevant portion of
the same reads as under:-
ìWe, while upholding the aforesaid view,
substitute our own opinion by laying down that even
though a transfer order on administrative ground per
se is not bad in law, no person can be transferred on
an administrative ground unless before issuing the
transfer order, the Authority competent to transfer
has arrived at and recorded his satisfaction, upon
due verification and confirmation, about the existence
and truthfulness of any of the three
factors/grounds/considerations warranting the
transfer of the person concerned.î
3. From the perusal of the impugned order it is
clear that no reason has been assigned by the authority
concerned. Though in the counter affidavit it has been
stated that there was a complaint against the petitioner by
the Medical Superintendent, Community Health Centre,
Jaspur (respondent No. 4) as well as other persons of
Jaspur and on the basis of those complaints, the Chief
Medical Officer, Udham Singh Nagar passed the impugned
order of transfer.
4. Since there has been allegation of the petitioner
against the concerned Medical Officer i.e. respondent No.
4, he was present in person in this Court on 04.01.2014
when he was asked to file his counter affidavit, but no
counter affidavit has been filed by him as yet. The counter
affidavit filed by the State Authorities only states that there
are various complaints against the petitioner, which

3
compelled the authorities to the transfer her from
Community Health Centre, Jaspur to Community Health
Centre, Khatima. It is absolutely clear from the perusal of
the impugned order that no reason has been assigned for
transferring the petitioner on the Administrative ground by
the authority concerned, therefore, this order is liable to be
quashed.
5. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed. The
impugned order dated 20/22.08.2013 is hereby quashed.
6. This Court has been informed that the
petitioner, in pursuance to the transfer order, has joined
Community Health Centre, Khatima on 13.01.2014, the
respondents are directed to give joining to the petitioner at
Community Health Centre, Jaspur forthwith.
7. However, the respondents are at liberty to pass
an order but while doing so, they must assign reasons of
such transfer, in the light of the Full Bench decision of this
Court, referred above.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
13.03.2014
ASWAL
